title: DecodeSidecar
description: A decode report and source fidelity bound to exact CADIR bytes.

fidelity.description: Decode-time annotations and retained source records.

ir_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the exact CADIR bytes this sidecar describes.

ir_version.description: Exact IR wire version shared with the CADIR document.

Admission.description:
How one format layer admitted, or refused, one document.

Identity and admission are orthogonal: a document can carry a registry row
of its own while its bytes are read with another grammar, and a damaged
frame can retain its identity while applying that row's grammar
unverified. The grammar name is local to the owning [`DialectMatch`]'s
format namespace.

oneOf.description: Parsed with the strategy declared for the identified dialect.

Parsed with another declared grammar of the same format namespace.

The codec must charge its dialect-unverified loss.

using.description: Format-local name of the grammar the parser applied.

oneOf.description:
Parsed without any declared grammar: the residual path.

The codec must charge its dialect-unverified loss.
Structurally identified; semantic decode refused.

Annotations.description:
Document-wide provenance and exactness tables keyed by globally unique
entity id.

An entity absent from `exactness` is byte-exact.

provenance.description: Source location for each annotated entity.

coverage.description: Decode coverage counts keyed by declared measure name.

identity.description: Source format identity and its classified dialect layers.

transfer_ledger.description: Per-source disposition ledger for decoded records and entities.

DecodeTransfer.description:
Mutually exclusive source-transfer states for a decode report.

The backend reports the state it delivered; the sealed decode wrapper
records its [`depth`](Self::depth) on the document.

oneOf.description:
The decoder stopped after container inspection and transferred no
semantic geometry.

The decoder transferred the model and left every design arena empty,
with the recorded B-rep geometry outcome.

geometry_transferred.description: Whether B-rep geometry was transferred into the IR.

oneOf.description:
The decoder transferred the model and its design and left every
process arena empty, with the recorded B-rep geometry outcome.

geometry_transferred.description: Whether B-rep geometry was transferred into the IR.

oneOf.description:
The decoder transferred the model and its design, with the recorded
B-rep geometry outcome.

geometry_transferred.description: Whether B-rep geometry was transferred into the IR.

DialectId.description:
A registry dialect id, for example `"rhino:archive-80"`.

Canonical form is `<format>:<name>`. The format contains lowercase ASCII
letters and digits. The name also admits dots and hyphens, but a hyphen
cannot be first or last. Outside the owning codec the validated id is an
opaque label.

Serializes and deserializes as the plain string. Read it with
[`DialectId::as_str`] or print it; there is no other access to the raw
string.

DialectLayers.description:
A report's primary format layer and any nested or carried format layers.

Extra layers are unique by `(format, instance)`. An extra layer for the
primary format has an instance that identifies it inside the containing
document. The wire names the primary explicitly, so the collection carries
its complete identity without an enclosing report's format.

A read rejects a wire whose `extra` repeats a `(format, instance)` key, and
one whose `extra` carries the primary key. The key set on the wire is the
key set of the value, so no layer is silently discarded or overwritten.

DialectMatch.description:
One format layer's identification of one document.

A document carries several format layers: `.sldprt` contains Parasolid;
`.f3d`, `.ipt`, and SAT contain ACIS; NX contains Parasolid and JT. One
match describes one layer.

declared.description:
Version fields the source declared, verbatim, under keys pinned per
codec in the registry.

Declarations are evidence, never a control input: the dialect is what
the bytes obey, not what they declare.

instance.description:
Instance of this format layer inside the containing document.

`None` when the layer occurs once or has no report-local identity. This
is not source-declared evidence and therefore does not belong in
[`Self::declared`].

Exactness.description: How an entity or field value was established from its source.

oneOf.description:
Read verbatim from the source stream with no transformation beyond
documented unit conversion.
Computed deterministically from byte-exact inputs.
Filled in from context or convention rather than an explicit source field.
Origin or trustworthiness could not be established.

ExactnessNote.description: Exactness for an entity and sparse overrides for its serialized fields.

oneOf.description: The entity itself is not byte-exact; listed fields override it.

entity.description: Exactness of the entity except where overridden by `fields`.

fields.description: Exactness overrides keyed by serde field path.

oneOf.description: The entity is byte-exact apart from the listed fields.

fields.description: Exactness overrides keyed by serde field path.

FormatIdentity.description:
A format identity that is either classified by a typed payload or retains
only its known format.

Classified state stores no second format string. The payload is the one
author of its namespace, so the format is on the wire exactly once in
either state.

oneOf.description: The payload carries the complete classified identity.

dialects.description: Classified payload, whose namespace is the format.

oneOf.description: The format is known but no classification payload exists.

Grammar.description:
Format-local name of a dialect grammar, for example `sch-sw-33103`.

The namespace is the owning [`DialectMatch`]'s, so a grammar cannot name a
foreign format by construction. The name holds the character class a
[`DialectId`] admits after its separator, which excludes the separator
itself: a full id has no spelling as a grammar name.

Serializes and deserializes as the plain string. `try_from` is the mint, so
no read path reaches the field without the check. serde refuses
`transparent` beside `try_from`; a newtype struct writes its inner string
with no wrapper of its own, which is the same wire form.

Inexactness.description: Exactness of an entity that is not byte-exact.

oneOf.description: Computed deterministically from byte-exact inputs.
Filled in from context or convention rather than an explicit source field.
Origin or trustworthiness could not be established.

LossKind.description:
Machine-readable loss code on the decode/export wire.

A `kind` tag selects the variant. A shared loss is
`{ "kind": "shared", "value": { "kind": "pcurve_omitted" } }`; a codec-local
one is `{ "kind": "namespaced", "value": { "namespace": "rhino", "code":
"brep.trim-pcurve-dropped", "kind": "pcurve_omitted" } }`, carrying
`strict_floor` exactly when the code pins one.

oneOf.description: Shared loss whose wire code is determined by its taxonomy.

kind.description: Shared taxonomy, which is also the local code.

oneOf.description: Codec-local loss with an independently pinned strict-mode floor.

LossNamespaceName.description: An owned loss namespace other than the reserved shared namespace.

LossNote.description: One attributable instance of incomplete or approximate transfer.

count.description: The number of source instances the note reports together.

provenance.description: Where in the source the loss occurred, when attributable.

LossTaxonomy.description:
Shared cross-codec loss taxonomy.

Category and default severity live here. Codec-local loss enums map into a
taxonomy variant for subsystem reporting; strict-mode floors on a
[`LossKind`] are pinned at construction so a later local→taxonomy remap in
source does not silently change rejection.

oneOf.description:
No geometry stream was located in the container, so no B-rep could be
transferred.

The B-rep topology graph was not transferred, though carriers or a
container were decoded.

The source topology violates a neutral topology invariant; the decoder
reported the defect and retained only valid neutral topology.

B-rep geometry was not transferred, though carriers or a container were
decoded.
Geometric agreement was checked at sampled parameters only.

A reference graph decoded but did not close into a consistent
surface/pcurve/edge/vertex binding.

Face sense, body kind, or a body/region/shell hierarchy was supplied by
a deterministic gauge because the source fields were unresolved.

A carrier axis, plane, or orientation was inferred from adjacent
carriers rather than read from a source field.
Informational carrier or record census; no content was lost.
Materials or appearances were not transferred.
Document, feature, or part metadata was not transferred.
Attributes (names, colors, custom attributes) were not transferred.

Named feature operations and their dependency tables were retained as
native passthrough rather than replayed.

The part is an assembly; component geometry lives in external referenced
files, not inline.
Assembly component occurrence placements were not transferred.
A record was decoded but yielded no typed IR entity.

A decode-time diagnostic surfaced as a loss note; detail is in the
message.
Stored integrity data does not match the bytes it protects.
The source uses a recoverable but noncanonical serialization.

The source declares a dialect or specification version whose semantics
the decoder has not verified for that declaration.

The writer emitted a different dialect from the source dialect, so the
source dialect identity was not preserved.

Standalone mesh vertices were stored at reduced (f32) precision by the
source archive.
Some source object records were not transferred to typed IR.
An object family or class is not supported and was not transferred.
A named source asset (geometry, material, or other) was not transferred.

The IR contained no exportable solids, so the target representation is
empty.
Hidden bodies were omitted from the exported output.

A body's non-identity transform was not applied; coordinates are written
in body-local space.

Signed or self-intersecting analytic surfaces were normalized to the
target's positive-radius convention.
Elliptical cones were reduced to circular conical carriers.
Edges without a typed 3D curve were omitted from their edge loops.
Faces resting on an unknown surface were omitted from the exported shell.
Parameter-space pcurves were not written; consumers recompute trims.

Subdivision surfaces were omitted because the writer does not encode
control cages.
Tessellations were omitted because the writer emits exact geometry only.
Point clouds were not represented in the target.
Product-manufacturing-information annotations were not represented in the target.
Source-object associations were not represented in the target.
Uninterpreted passthrough records were not represented in the target.

Procedural surface or curve definitions were reduced to their solved
carriers.
Parametric design or history records were not represented in the target.

Appearance assets were reduced to base colors; schemas, textures, and
shader properties were dropped.
Preserved source bytes required for a byte-exact write were unavailable.

Physical materials, mass properties, rigid bodies, colliders, or joint
drives were not transferred.

Manufacturing process records (setups, operations, tools, programs,
toolpaths, or process states) were not represented in the target.

NamespacedLossKind.description:
Codec-local loss identity and classification.

Fields are private so the reserved `shared` namespace can be constructed
only as [`LossKind::Shared`].

strict_floor.description: Strict-mode severity floor pinned by this code; absent when it has none.

RetainedBytes.description:
The retained image of a source record: its bytes, or the length and digest
of bytes that are not retained.

oneOf.description:
The source bytes themselves. Their length and digest are functions of
them, so neither is stored.
Unavailable source bytes, described by their length and digest.

sha256.description: Lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the source bytes.

RetainedSourceRecord.description:
Source bytes retained for native recovery or replay.

The record is addressed by its id in
[`SourceFidelity::retained_records`], so it carries no id of its own.

bytes.description: Retained image of the source bytes.

offset.description: First byte offset in the source stream.

untyped.description:
Content classes the bytes can hold where the decoder keeps the record
without decoding it.

Severity.description: Severity of a loss note or validation finding.

oneOf.description: Informational; no action needed.
Non-fatal approximation or normalization.
A correctness problem in the produced IR or export.
A hard stop: the requested operation cannot be completed faithfully.

annotations.description: Sparse source locations and conversion exactness.

codec_digests.description:
The decoding codec's narrower digests, keyed as its format
specification lists.

content_digest.description: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the document the decode returned.

decode_digest.description: SHA-256 of the decode's root file.

file_digests.description: SHA-256 of each component file, keyed by its `File` definition.

retained_records.description: Native records retained for recovery or replay, keyed by record id.

unrepresented.description: Union of the retained records' untyped classes.

TransferLedger.description: Complete source-to-result accounting for a decode.

entries.description: Entries in deterministic source traversal order.

TransferOutcome.description:
One source object's structurally valid transfer outcome.

The disposition is the wire's tag, so each outcome carries exactly the
fields valid for it: an emitted record has no note to state, and an omitted
record has no target.

oneOf.description: Transferred as an exact neutral or native entity.
Preserved in a native retained-record arena.

note.description: Informational note about retention or semantic projection.

oneOf.description: Transferred with an explicit approximation.
Deliberately not transferred.

outcome.description: Outcome whose variant carries exactly the data valid for its disposition.

source.description: Stable source identity or source-local record key.
